filing-20260803-5210.point: The NYTOs file independently under section 3.10(a) of the NYISO-TO Agreement, which lets each TO file section 205 changes to recover costs and for retail access.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: section 3.10(a) confers upon each Transmission Owner the unilateral right to file with the Commission under FPA section 205

filing-20260803-5210.point: They plan a cost recovery mechanism coordinated with the NYPSC, likely a pro forma agreement or tariff provisions.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: The NYTOs intend to incorporate the NYPSC's cost allocation determinations and to file with the Commission a proposed mechanism

filing-20260803-5210.point: Possible terms include a minimum financial contribution plus security to protect other customers if the load does not take the expected service.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: Such arrangements may include a minimum financial contribution from the large load customer or Eligible Customer, as applicable, toward the Transmission Owner's transmission revenue requirement

filing-20260803-5210.point: They will provide revenue credits where upgrade costs paid by a large load are also in rates paid by other customers.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: the NYTO will provide for a revenue credit to the extent the NYTO is recovering those Network Upgrade costs.

filing-20260803-5210.point: NYISO's planned Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would need changes to billing determinants and cost allocation.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: The different forms of service may require changes in the billing determinants, billing units, demand allocators, and cost allocation mechanisms.

filing-20260803-5210.point: The NYTOs will address Facilities Study process, timeline and evaluation of alternative transmission technologies in the section 205 filing.
filing-20260803-5210.quote: the NYTOs intend to address whether and how the Facilities Study process should require evaluation of alternative transmission technologies

filing-20260803-5241.point: The NTOs seek a 90-day full abeyance to prepare a section 205 filing alongside NYISO and stakeholders.
filing-20260803-5241.quote: The NTOs seek a 90-day full abeyance of the current 60-day deadline to respond to all issues raised in the Show Cause Order

filing-20260803-5241.point: They expect the filing to cover large load definition, alternative transmission technologies, a pro forma service agreement, and cost recovery with financial security.
filing-20260803-5241.quote: the definition of a large load; readiness and information requirements; the

filing-20260803-5241.point: They say their section 205 filing depends on NYISO's stakeholder process because NTOs run no stakeholder process of their own.
filing-20260803-5241.quote: NTOs do not administer a stakeholder process of their own through which the issues raised in the Show Cause Order could be resolved independently.

filing-20260803-5241.point: Without a shortened answer period, FERC could not rule before the August 17 response deadline.
filing-20260803-5241.quote: If the ordinary fifteen-day answer period applies, the Commission will not be in a position to rule on this Motion until after NTOs' response is already due.

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: NYISO requests the full 90 days and action by August 13.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: hold this proceeding in abeyance for the maximum period permitted by the Show Cause Order, i.e., for 90 days, until November 16, 2026.

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: NYISO plans a new large load study process replacing its existing load interconnection rules, with expedited joint studies.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: the NYISO plans to create a new large load study process that would replace and improve upon its existing load interconnection rules.

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: NYISO would offer firm and non-firm variants of its financial reservation service, with non-firm withdrawal service for flexible large loads.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: make large loads eligible to take non-firm withdrawal service to the extent their ability to be flexible mitigates their impact on the system.

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: For co-location, NYISO intends to sunset its BTM:NG program and treat load and generation as separate market entities.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: the NYISO intends to propose sunsetting its BTM:NG program and replacing it with a new co-located resource participation model

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: NYISO ties the timing to New York's shared governance and the NYPSC's parallel large-load proceeding.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: a 90-day abeyance is reasonable in the NYISO's case because it will facilitate the NYISO's ability to obtain approval from its stakeholder Management Committee before making a section 205 filing.

motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.point: Schedule: committee votes October 14 and 15, Management Committee October 28, filing November 16, 2026.
motion-el26-69-nyiso-abeyance.quote: Provided that Management Committee and Board approvals are secured, the NYISO will submit a section 205 proposal on November 16, 2026

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: NYISO says its existing markets and planning processes remain available even though large load growth presents challenges.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: the NYISO's markets and existing planning processes remain available to address resource adequacy.

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: Preliminary 2026 RNA results could show a statewide resource adequacy violation from 2033, exceeding 1,800 MW by 2036 with large load growth.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: the NYISO could identify a statewide resource adequacy criterion violation that would first occur in 2033 and increase through 2036 with a deficiency greater than 1,800 MW

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: The interconnection queue holds 89 completed projects over 11 GW awaiting operation and a 91-project, 15 GW transition cluster.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: the New York region has 89 projects, representing over 11 GW of generation, that have completed the interconnection study process but have yet to enter commercial operation.

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: For regulated generation solutions, the NYPSC decides cost allocation, including for shortfalls caused by a large load.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: The allocation of the costs for the development of the regulated generation or demand response solution would be determined by the NYPSC

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: NYISO is discussing an accelerated interconnection study path for resources needed to address an identified reliability need.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: a proposal to establish an accelerated interconnection study path for resources that are needed to address a reliability need

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: NYISO is considering assigning responsibility for a resource deficiency to a large load that directly contributes to it.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: If the NYISO identifies a resource deficiency and the large load(s) directly contributes to such deficiency, then the NYISO is considering assigning the

report-el26-69-nyiso.point: Planning reforms would go to committees in January to March 2027, with a section 205 filing around March 2027.
report-el26-69-nyiso.quote: with a filing submitted to the Commission under Section 205 of the FPA in or around March 2027, subject to necessary approvals.
